subject: English
topic: Right Form of Verbs (৫০টি মাস্টার সেট)
exam_tips: লিখিত পরীক্ষায় সরাসরি ব্র্যাকেটে Verb দিয়ে শূন্যস্থান থাকে। Tense ও Subject-Verb Agreement খেয়াল করে উত্তর লিখুন।

items.question: He (go) to school yesterday.
items.rule: Past time markers like yesterday, ago take Past Indefinite.

items.question: It is high time we (change) our habits.
items.rule: It is high time + subject requires Past Indefinite.

items.question: I fancy I (turn) pale.
He speaks as if he (know) everything.
He speaks as though he (be) a scholar.
I look forward to (hear) from you soon.
He went to the library with a view to (read) books.
Scarcely had the teacher entered the room when the students (stand) up.
No sooner had he seen the police than he (run) away.
items.rule: No sooner had ... than + past indefinite.

items.question: Neither of the two boys (be) present.
items.rule: Neither of + plural noun takes singular verb.

items.question: The jury (be) unanimous in their opinion.
items.rule: Collective noun unanimous takes singular verb.

items.question: The jury (be) divided in their opinions.
items.rule: Noun of multitude takes plural verb.

items.question: One of the boys (be) absent yesterday.
The quality of these mangoes (be) not good.
Bread and butter (be) his favorite breakfast.
items.rule: Compound noun forming a single unit takes singular.

items.question: Slow and steady (win) the race.
Ten miles (be) a long distance to walk.
items.rule: Distance, money, time measurements take singular verb.

items.question: If you came, I (go).
items.rule: Second conditional: If + past indefinite, would + V1.

items.question: If he had studied hard, he (pass) the exam.
items.rule: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + V3.

items.question: Had I seen him, I (tell) him the news.
items.rule: Inverted third conditional: Had + S + V3, would have + V3.

items.question: He has just (finish) his assignment.
items.rule: Just, already take Present Perfect (has/have + V3).

items.question: I would rather starve than (beg).
You had better (leave) the place right now.
I saw the boy (play) in the field.
items.rule: Sensory verbs take participle for continuous action.

items.question: The earth (move) round the sun.
He talked as though he (know) everything.
I wish I (be) a king.
The train had started before I (reach) the station.
items.rule: Before clause in past perfect takes Simple Past.

items.question: While (walk) in the garden, a snake bit him.
While he (walk) in the morning, he saw an accident.
It (rain) since morning.
The bell (ring) before the teacher entered.
He cannot help (laugh) at the funny joke.
Do not get down from a (run) train.
The letter was (write) by him yesterday.
He made me (do) the work.
items.rule: Causative 'make' takes bare infinitive in active voice.

items.question: I was made (do) the work by him.
items.rule: Causative 'make' in passive voice takes full infinitive ('to do').

items.question: The patient died after the doctor (come).
Each of the students (receive) a medal.
Fifty thousand dollars (be) a large sum of money.
items.rule: Total sum of money takes singular verb.

items.question: The news (be) true.
The United States (be) a powerful country.
items.rule: Country names ending in 's' take singular verb.

items.question: Water (freeze) at 0 degree Celsius.
Had you invited me, I (attend) the function.
Lest he should (fail), he worked hard.
Run fast lest you (miss) the train.
He (live) in Dhaka for five years.
items.rule: Action continuing over a period takes Present Perfect Continuous.

items.question: The virtuous (be) always happy.
items.rule: 'The' + adjective representing plural class takes plural verb.

items.question: By this time tomorrow, I (reach) my village.
items.rule: Future perfect: 'By + future time' requires will have + V3.

items.question: Let him (do) whatever he likes.
The mother made the baby (drink) the milk.
I had my car (repair) yesterday.
items.rule: Causative 'have' with passive object takes V3.

items.question: He got his hair (cut) at the salon.
items.rule: Causative 'get' with passive object takes V3.

items.question: I cannot help (shed) tears at his grief.
He went away (weep).
Would you mind (open) the window?
items.rule: 'Would you mind' is followed by gerund.

items.question: It is no use (cry) over spilt milk.
There is no harm in (try) again.
He gave up (smoke) last month.
He avoided (meet) the landlord.
He admitted (steal) the watch.
I finished (write) the essay just now.
The boy was punished for (tell) a lie.
He insisted on (go) with us.
He is fond of (read) historical novels.
I prevented him from (fall).
He succeeded in (secure) the first prize.
He went home after he (complete) his shift.
items.rule: 'After' clause in past takes Past Perfect.

items.question: Before the doctor came, the patient (die).
items.rule: Action completed before another past action takes Past Perfect.

items.question: Since 2010, they (live) in this neighborhood.
items.rule: Action continuing from past takes Present Perfect Continuous.

items.question: By the end of this year, he (serve) the office for twenty years.
If you had told me earlier, I (help) you.
Had I known his address, I (write) to him.
Unless you work hard, you (fail).
He walks fast as though he (be) in a hurry.
He stopped (write) when the bell rang.
The house needs (paint).
I cannot help (pity) the poor child.
He preferred reading to (write).
He had better (consult) an expert physician.
It is many years since I (meet) him.
Many years had passed since we first (meet).
He walked slowly lest he (stumble).
I wish I (have) a car.
items.rule: Unreal present wish takes Past Indefinite.

items.question: The principal desired that the meeting (be) postponed.
Hardly had he reached the stop when the bus (leave).
The thief was seen (enter) the building.
He spent the whole afternoon (play) chess.
I would rather die than (surrender).
If you boil water to 100 degrees, it (evaporate).
